h1: Mayrhofen ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Mayrhofen sits at 633 metres in the Zillertal, with 142 kilometres of pistes and 61 lifts above it across Ahorn, Penken, Finkenberg, Rastkogel and Eggalm. The Penken side holds the Harakiri, which the operator calls Austria's steepest slope experience at a 78% gradient, and the PenkenPark; Ahorn is the wide, sunny side, with a 5.5 kilometre black valley run dropping more than 1,300 metres back to the village.
stayOverview: The village is the base for both mountains: the Penkenbahn and the Ahornbahn leave from Mayrhofen itself, and a free ski bus runs to the Horberg and Mosl lifts. Finkenberg and Hippach are quieter and cheaper, on the same lift network.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. Staying in Mayrhofen means walking to a gondola; the neighbouring villages need the ski bus.
rentalCars: Mayrhofen is at the head of the Zillertal, about an hour from Innsbruck and reachable by the Zillertalbahn railway from Jenbach.

highlights.text: A 5.5 kilometre black run with more than 1,300 metres of descent, open from 7.30 a.m.

verticalDrop.unannounced: Mayrhofner Bergbahnen publishes a descent figure for a single run - 1,300 m on the ValleyRun Ahorn - but no vertical drop for the ski area.

topElevation.unannounced: No top elevation is published for the ski area. The 2,227 m the operator names is the summit of a winter hiking path on Mount Ahorn, not the top of the lift system.

season.note: The Ahornbahn opens a week later, on 12 December.

baseElevation.unannounced: The lift company's winter pages give the piste kilometres and the lift count and speak of three-thousand-metre peaks, but state no valley-station altitude.

longestRun.note: Our pick of the operator's own published run lengths - it marks the Ahorn valley run at 5.5 km down to the valley but does not label any run as its longest.

dayPass.note: The full-day ticket for the Mayrhofen ski area, including 10% VAT. Later starts cost less at the cash desk: EUR 74.00 from 11.00, EUR 61.50 from 12.00 and EUR 41.00 from 14.00.

facts.text: The Harakiri is Austria's steepest slope experience at a 78% gradient, and the Penken side adds the DevilsRun and BlackAttack.
Mount Ahorn is built around wide, sun-drenched carving slopes, the FunRide arena and the KinderLand Horberg beginner area.
PenkenPark has five areas, used by the international freeski and snowboard scene and open to beginners on the smaller kickers.

unannounced.statement: Mayrhofner Bergbahnen publishes 142 km of pistes but no split by difficulty on its winter or mountain pages.
